Woodbury Town Court

Address: 511 NY-32, Highland Mills, NY 10930, United States

Phone: 845-928-2311

Woodbury Town Court is a city and justice courthouse in the county of Orange, New York. It is located in the 2nd and 9th Judicial District Departments. This court has jurisdiction over the case of civil, criminal, small claims and traffic, and vehicle matters that happen within the Town. It also handles speeding tickets from the big roads and supermall. Court sessions were held every Tuesday and Wednesday after 5:00 pm. Proper dressing is required during the hearing.

The Woodbury Town Court is a local court located in the town of Woodbury, New York. It is part of the New York State Unified Court System and has jurisdiction over a variety of legal matters. The court is presided over by a town justice who is elected by the people of Woodbury.

What Cases Does the Woodbury Town Court Handle?

The Woodbury Town Court has jurisdiction over several types of legal matters, including:

  • Traffic Violations: The court handles traffic tickets and other traffic-related offenses, such as driving under the influence (DUI) and reckless driving.
  • Criminal Cases: The court can hear misdemeanor criminal cases, such as petit larceny and assault. However, it cannot handle felony cases.
  • Civil Cases: The court can handle civil disputes that involve amounts of up to $3,000. Examples of civil cases include small claims, landlord-tenant disputes, and breach of contract.

What Are the Procedures of the Woodbury Town Court?

If you have a legal issue that falls under the jurisdiction of the Woodbury Town Court, you will need to follow certain procedures. Here are the basic steps:

  1. Filing a Complaint: If you are the plaintiff in a civil case, you will need to file a complaint with the court. The court will then issue a summons to the defendant, notifying them of the legal action against them.
  2. Answering the Complaint: If you are the defendant, you will need to file an answer to the complaint within a certain period of time. Failure to do so could result in a default judgment against you.
  3. Pre-Trial Conference: In some cases, the court may hold a pre-trial conference to discuss the case with the parties involved. This is an opportunity to settle the case before going to trial.
  4. Trial: If the case cannot be settled, it will go to trial. The judge will hear evidence and make a decision based on the facts of the case.
  5. Sentencing: If the defendant is found guilty, the judge will impose a sentence. This could include fines, community service, or even jail time.

What Should You Bring to the Woodbury Town Court?

If you have a court date at the Woodbury Town Court, there are several things you should bring with you:

  • Your Summons or Ticket: You will need to bring the summons or ticket that was issued to you by the police officer or court.
  • Identification: You will need to bring a valid form of identification, such as a driver's license or passport.
  • Any Relevant Documents: If you have any documents that relate to your case, such as contracts or receipts, bring them with you.
  • Witnesses: If you have witnesses who can testify on your behalf, bring them with you.

How to Contact the Woodbury Town Court?

If you need to contact the Woodbury Town Court for any reason, you can use the following information:

  • Address: 511 Route 32, P.O. Box 1004, Highland Mills, NY 10930
  • Phone Number: (845) 928-2188
  • Email Address: woodburytcourt@nycourts.gov

How to search for the case record?

Woodbury Town Court records information for any case is available at the court office in files, on the computer, and online. The case search can be online in the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

The person can see any records of legal and court documents. However, information for matrimonial or sealed records is not accessible to the public because they are confidential and sealed by the law. The action parties and the attorney of the record can only access the matrimonial records information. For criminal records search, you had to submit the criminal record access form to the clerk's office. For divorce and family matters case information, contact the family court. If you are copying the ordered documents, give the index number, filing date, and record type you sought, and give the parties or business name. The record search is free, but the copying fee is $0.25 per copy.

Division

Woodbury Town Court division consists of the following:

  • Criminal Division
  • Civil Division
  • Traffic Division
  • Small Claim Division

How much fine is given on a traffic violation?

Municipal Court">Campbell Municipal Court traffic violation fines depend on your type of violation. For speed violations over the 15-19 speed limit, the total fine and cost will be $158; for driving while the license is expired, the fine and expense you had to pay is $163.The total fine and cost for disobeying a stop sign twice a month are $188.The total fine and reckless driving charge two times a month are $178.Fail to yield total fine and cost is $158. Using Local Street will result in a $178 total fine and cost. $163 is the full fine and cost if you drive a motor vehicle in an open container. Suppose you drive without a seat belt; you must pay $104.

How to make payments?

Woodbury Town Court traffic tickets and other fines payment can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can pay for traffic tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the counter. 2.99% convenience and other charges will be applied if you pay with a credit card.

Online

A person can make an online payment using www.WoodburyCourtPayments.com . Enter the traffic ticket number and pay with any credit card or mastercard. Processing fees will be applied to the online payment system.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 511 NY-32, Highland Mills, NY 10930, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted.

The traffic court handles which types of cases?

The Town of Woodbury Traffic Court handles cases of traffic and vehicle violations. The violation includes speeding, accidents, using cell phones while driving, failing to follow a traffic signal or traffic control device, driving with a suspended or no license, leaving the scene of the accident, and driving recklessly. It also handles speeding ticket cases given by the sheriff or New York Police on the busy roads. Enter a plea of guilty or not guilty and send it to court. The court will respond whether to appear in court or pay the fine. Hire a professional traffic Ticket attorney for traffic and speeding cases because they can defend you against the traffic charges in court.

How to file a small claim case?

The Town of Woodbury Small Claims Court handles cases in which the claim is up to $3000. To file a small claim case, a person had to come to the court during business hours and fill out the form. You had to write in the form the reason for claiming and the amount you are suing. The person and company involved in the case must be from this Town.

What is the role of a clerk?

The Town Of Woodbury Court clerk's role is to help the judges, take payments, manage files, provide certificates and licenses like marriage licenses, birth and death certificate copy, manage public records, vital statistics, landlord registration, and custody of documents. The clerk acts as an administrative official and a secretary to the governing body. They are an agent of licensing and custodians of the town records. They also record the proceeding of the Town Board Meeting entirely and accurately.

How to get a marriage license?

Woodbury Town Court's marriage license is obtained from the clerk's office and is provided by Monroe County. The fee for a marriage license is $40 and for certificates is $10 per copy. The couple's age must be 18+. The couple had to bring an original birth certificate with a certified copy and a photo ID that proves their identification, like a driver's license. If this is anyone's second marriage, a divorce paper or spouse's death certificate must be required at the time of registration. If anyone wants copies, fill out the marriage research application, and submit it to the court. It is valid for up to 60 days. A person has to make an appointment when they want a marriage license. You had to apply for a permit 24 hours before the marriage ceremony; after the ceremony is completed, the couple will get an original marriage certificate.

Conclusion

The Woodbury Town Court is an important legal institution for the people of Woodbury, New York. Whether you have a traffic ticket, a criminal case, or a civil dispute, the court has the jurisdiction to hear your case. By understanding the procedures and requirements of the court, you can better prepare yourself for your court date and increase your chances of a positive outcome.

FAQ:

How would I know how much fine I had to pay after receiving a traffic ticket?

The amount is not decided; you have to send a plea of guilty or not guilty, and then the court will send you a notice of how much fine you had to pay.

What are the fees for birth and death certificate copies?

$10 per copy is the fee for birth and death certificates.

What proof of ID should I submit to the court for identification in the marriage certificate?

The proof of ID that will be accepted for identification are:

  • Driver's License
  • Passport
  • Employee ID
  • Military ID

What happens if I do not pay the fine on time?

License and insurance will be suspended if you do not pay the fine on time.

How to contact the clerk's office?

Visit the clerk's office regularly or call them for any information or guidance.
